scope: Independent requested-byte/count admission for the five global capability, IPC, completion, mailbox-capability and mailbox-word namespace map nodes, including empty preparation, detached storage and terminal retention.

policy.decision: Count limits allow twice the five-node needs at complete-root capacity, retaining overlap/replacement/quarantine headroom and a quarter trusted reserve. Current five layouts hit count before byte ceilings even for the largest type; requested-byte admission independently bounds future layout growth. No existing resource ceiling is increased or RAM preallocated.
policy.cost: The node carries a requested-byte count and immutable original-class flag. Reuse existing typed admitted maps and retirement owners; do not combine account or nested payload charges with global node lifetime.
policy.classification: Same unpublished-root or exact-generation trusted translation-storage capture used by account preparation; metadata reserve grants no resource privileges and later promotion cannot reclassify existing nodes.

controls: Actual empty capability-layout nodes fill ordinary and total count ceilings. Oversized synthetic layouts reject on requested bytes with count headroom, before allocator entry. Sixty-four heap-held ordinary denials and trusted total denial precede allocation.

Capability preparation rejects at ordinary exhaustion; one free slot permits capability storage but rejects IPC preparation. Exact node/account/frame/root counts recover before ASID publication. Completion replacement and new mailbox candidates reject while existing receiver and established word queues remain usable.

Trusted root plus completion/mailbox/word initialization consumes five reserved nodes at ordinary exhaustion. Existing IPC and mailbox adapters still use ordinary resource admission before a grant. Later promotion changes neither original node bytes nor refund class.

Root close at total exhaustion returns exactly five original ordinary nodes and 552 requested bytes. Fresh root initialization consumes exactly that recovered allowance, then closes and all pressure storage returns to baseline.

Each of five actual layouts has 64 injected allocation rejections (320 total) with exact counter recovery. Existing IPC and completion publications/removals run under actual heap/node-pool guards and finish outside them.

Existing capability, IPC, completion, mailbox and containing root preparation/retirement abandonment controls hold the new node pool. Four standalone retained IPC nodes keep original bytes/count; no new deliberate-retention fixture is added.

Failed final-root invalidation retains its captured capability namespace node. Confirmation refunds its original bytes/count independently of intervening root creation; terminal quarantine preserves storage.
Existing allocator-traced retirement-collection host controls qualify payload/node disposal, post-deallocation charge release and retaining fallback.
qualification_limits: Pressure uses actual empty capability-layout nodes, not the largest mixed footprint or maximum nested resource payloads. Current byte-denial tests deliberately use oversized synthetic layouts; current production count ceilings bind first.
The pool covers requested node layouts, not allocator overhead, independently surviving accounts/payloads, aggregate principal use or general kernel heap.

Native heap exhaustion is not forced; five-layout allocation errors use named injection controls. No sustained hostile concurrent EL0 pressure fairness, per-service entitlement, worst-case global lookup/IRQ latency or physical hardware guarantee.

Individual payload/registry nodes outside the five global maps, Waker/callback and other observer storage, aggregate principal/general-heap admission and the wider cleanup/destructor inventory remain open. SEC-07 remains partial; existing C02/C03/C10/C18 and G1/G4 boundaries remain.
